decision: The verify:ac verified > 0 requirement binds only when at least one walked clause is bound to an artifact path (adjudicable > 0); a zero-failed clause set with no bound paths passes.

governingRule.description: #3826 bound remedy 2 (fix the ok predicate); #3156 gate integrity; #3265 thin fail-closed design

alternativesConsidered.option: Scope the conjunct by AcceptanceReaderProfile so task check relaxes it and scope:complete keeps it
Exclude source_rung: derived clause sets from the committability gate entirely
Stop stamping derived clauses when plan.items already declares the acceptance surface
Leave the conjunct alone and split the durability defect into a separate issue

whyWinner: A clause with no bound artifact path can only ever return unverifiable, so requiring a positive verified from such a set is unsatisfiable by correct work; the only way to pass it was the absent-artifact false positive that remedy 1 removes. Keying on adjudicable keeps the done-time standard wherever the walk actually has an oracle, unlike profile scoping (which would leave standalone verify:ac and pre-pr still blocked) or a blanket source_rung exemption (which drops the standard even where paths are bound). Non-path criteria remain gated by evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate at scope:complete.
revisitTrigger: If artifact_path shape validation lands (critic A finding 5 / #3835) so derived clauses reliably bind real paths, adjudicable would approach walked and the carve-out would stop mattering; revisit also if a brief is observed passing with zero bound paths and no per-item evidence.
